note: Ratchet for `scripts/loc-metrics.py`. Every number below is lines of git-tracked source, classified by the lexer in `scripts/lib/loc_classify.py`. They may only go DOWN — raising a limit to make a build green defeats the point of measuring, so a rise fails the gate. When a rise is deliberate, run `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline` and commit the new file in the SAME commit that grew the tree. Generated files (`@generated` / `DO NOT EDIT` in the header) are measured but excluded from these limits, because appending a wire kind must never fail a size gate. The `*.comment` numbers are measured and diffed but NOT gated: a gate that makes deleting documentation the cheapest way to go green is pointed at the wrong thing. What these limits do NOT cover, stated so the total has a denominator: the programme's own tooling, 11 `.py` files (3,434 code lines) and 25 `.sh` files (3,821), 7,255 code lines in all -- roughly 4.4% of the tree, and rising, because this tooling is inside its own blind spot. Counting them needs a `#`-comment lexer for two more languages, here-documents and docstrings included, and until that exists moving logic into a script still reads as reduction.
measured:
2026-08-10 on branch `feat/foreign-write-bridge-#176`, stacked on `feat/cross-folia-region-commit-#179` (PR #260), by `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline`. Read this field before assuming a rise was lazy.

The rise is +563 java.main.code, +327 java.test.code and +6 kotlin.main.code, and all of it is server task 8 deliverables 2-4 -- the plugin-side foreign-write bridge (issue #176, L-65). Three new production classes in `endpoints/paper-plugin/.../compat` (`ForeignWriteBridge`, `BukkitForeignWrites`, `WorldEditBulkWrites`) plus `NoderaRegionDeniedEvent`, the enable-time wiring in `NoderaEndpointPlugin`, one new suite (`ForeignWriteBridgeTest`, 9 tests) and three new stages in `PluginsScenario` (C3/C4/C5). The Kotlin lines are the EngineHub repository and the WorldEdit `compileOnly` in that module's build script.

**Why there are two Bukkit adapters and not one.** `//set` fires NO Bukkit block event: WorldEdit writes straight down its own extent pipeline. A bridge built on `BlockPlaceEvent` alone reports "certified" for a hand-placed block and observes nothing at all for the bulk operation L-65's exit clause names, which is a green test that asserts nothing. `WorldEditBulkWrites` is the second feed, and its line count is the cost of that clause being real. Verified on a real Paper 1.21.1-133: 1,280 of 1,280 blocks observed.

The test half is deliberately smaller than the production half here, the opposite of #179's shape, because the decisive evidence for this row is a LIVE run rather than a headless one -- `ForeignWriteBridgeTest` covers the decision table and the denial payload, and the bulk path can only be proven by a real WorldEdit.

Every bucket sits exactly on its measured value, because that is what `--baseline` writes; there is never any headroom, so a one-line fix and its test cost a stamp. That pressure is the known cost of an exact ratchet, and the answer to it is a reason recorded here, not a limit with slack in it.
